settings.board.autoSyncHint: Periodically commits and pushes .git-manager/board.json for GitHub-backed boards, so column changes reach the team without a manual commit. Off by default — like force-push, this touches the repo on your behalf.
settings.ai.enabledHint: Turn AI features on. When off, AI-specific settings (like AI - commit) are hidden.
settings.ai.groupProviderHint: Where the model runs, and how to reach it.
settings.ai.groupModelsHint: The main model answers everything. A fast model is optional and only takes the per-file summaries.
settings.ai.groupLimitsHint: How long a request may take, and how much the model can read at once.
settings.ai.groupCommitStyleHint: How generated commit messages should read, on top of any commitlint config and the repository’s own history.
settings.ai.groupBriefingHint: The per-project recap the app writes on its own, and where it is archived.
settings.ai.timeoutHint: For a streamed answer this is how long to wait for the **first** token — prompt processing, the long part; once tokens flow, a 30 s silence is treated as a dead stream. For a one-shot answer (commit message, per-file summaries, history-search verdicts) it caps the whole generation. Runaway output is bounded by a token cap, not by this. An unreachable provider fails in seconds either way. Set it to 0 to wait as long as the model needs.
settings.ai.timeoutNone: No limit: a call waits until the model answers. Nothing else changes — an unreachable provider still fails in seconds, a dead stream is still cut, and output is still capped. Only the clock on a model that is working is gone, so a slow answer costs you time instead of costing you the result.
settings.ai.contextTokensHint: Your model's context size. Features size their prompts from this value, and a provider that receives more than it serves drops the START of the prompt — the instructions — without reporting it. Ollama picks its own default from your available memory (4096 on most machines), unless you raised it via a Modelfile or OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH. Check below rather than guessing.
settings.ai.concurrencyHint: How many model calls run at once when a feature reads a changeset file by file, or history commit by commit. Whether this helps is your server's decision, not the app's: one that serves a single generation at a time (Ollama's default) gains nothing, while one that batches gets faster — and each individual call gets SLOWER, so raise the timeout with it. Measure before trusting a number above 1.
settings.ai.extraBodyHint: Merged into every request your server receives, for the settings the OpenAI-compatible API does not standardise — above all switching a reasoning model's thinking off. There is no single spelling: `{"reasoning_effort": "none"}` is in the OpenAI spec, `{"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}` is what vLLM and Qwen document, `{"think": false}` is Ollama's. A field your server does not know usually means it rejects every call, so change one thing and test the connection.
settings.ai.extraBodyInvalid: Not a JSON object — nothing is saved until this parses. Wrap the fields in braces, for example { "reasoning_effort": "none" }.
settings.ai.contextCheckUnknown: The provider did not report a context length. Only Ollama does — for anything else this value cannot be checked, so keep it conservative.
settings.ai.contextCheckMax: The model supports up to {{max}} tokens.
settings.ai.contextCheckAllocated: The server currently serves it with a {{allocated}}-token window.
settings.ai.contextCheckServed: The provider reports it serves up to {{served}} tokens for this model.
settings.ai.contextCheckPlausible: Your value is plausible, but unconfirmed: the model isn't loaded, so the window the server would actually give it can't be seen. Run any AI feature, then check again.
settings.ai.contextCheckMatchesAllocated: Your value matches it — verified against what the server actually allocates, not just what the model supports.
settings.ai.contextCheckAboveAllocated: Your value of {{declared}} is above that: prompts will lose their start — the instructions — with nothing reported. Lower it to {{allocated}}, or raise OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH.
settings.ai.contextCheckBelowAllocated: Your value of {{declared}} is below that, so features read less of your changes than the server would allow. Raise it to {{allocated}}.
settings.ai.contextCheckBelowServed: Your value of {{declared}} is far below that, so features read only a fraction of your changes for no reason. Raise it to {{served}}.
settings.ai.contextCheckTooHigh: Your value of {{declared}} is above what the model supports: prompts will be silently truncated. Lower it.

settings.git.targetBranchesHelper: The branch this repo's work is merged into. The first one that exists in the repo is used.
settings.git.commitInstructionsPlacehold: e.g. Prefix with the ticket id; keep the subject under 60 chars; write in English…
settings.git.commitInstructionsHint: Guidance the AI follows when generating commit messages, on top of the repo's own commitlint config and history.
settings.git.commitPatternHint: Optional. Generated subjects that don't match are flagged with a warning.
settings.git.initialGraphCommitsHint: Minimum 500. If commit lazy loading is enabled, the App will load additional commits when you reach the earliest commit in the Graph.
settings.git.autoPrune: Auto-prune deleted remote branches on fetch

settings.repository.noRepo: Open a repository to configure its overrides.
settings.repository.worktree.defaultFile: Glob patterns for gitignored local files (.env, config…) copied from this repo into every new worktree. One pattern per line.
settings.repository.run.helper: Commands runnable from the toolbar's "Launch" button, executed in your external terminal at the repo directory. Star a task to make it the default.
settings.appearance.glassTransparency.hi: How much of the desktop shows through. The right setting depends on your wallpaper — a busy one competes with the commit graph.
settings.appearance.rowHeight.info: Height of every commit row in the graph: 32 px when small, 40 px when standard. The author avatar follows, at 24 px or 32 px.
settings.appearance.rowHeight.info.scope: Affects the commit graph only — side panels, file lists and the sidebar keep their own sizing.

settings.rewards.resetConfirm: Do you really want to reset ALL your accumulated achievements and XP? This action is irreversible.
settings.ai.dailySummary.enabledHint: Show an AI briefing per project in the launchpad, recapping yesterday's work and suggesting today's plan.
settings.ai.dailySummary.autoGenerateHin: Automatically refresh each project's briefing the first time you open the launchpad each day.
settings.ai.dailySummary.saveToRepoHint: Write a copy to .git-manager/summaries/ in each project, so the archive travels with it. The folder is added to .git/info/exclude, so the copies never appear as pending changes.
settings.ai.dailySummary.retentionHint: Briefings are markdown files under ~/.git-manager/summaries/, kept for 60 days.

settings.ai.presetHint.openaiCompatible: Any server speaking the OpenAI API (LM Studio, vLLM, MLX, OpenAI…). Set the URL yourself.
settings.ai.urlHint: API base URL. A bare host gets /v1 appended (http://localhost:11434 → …/11434/v1); give the full base yourself if your server uses another prefix (http://localhost:8000/v1).
settings.ai.apiKeyHint: Optional — only needed by providers that require a bearer token.

settings.ai.apiKeyStored: A key is saved in your keychain.
settings.ai.connectedNoModels: Connected, but the provider lists no model.
settings.ai.modelHint: Models are read from the provider's /v1/models endpoint. Validate the URL to refresh the list.
settings.ai.fastModelPlaceholder: e.g. a smaller model served by the same provider
settings.ai.fastModelHint: Used only for the per-file summaries, which run once per changed file and are the bulk of the wait on a large changeset. Everything that involves judgement — commit plans, history search verdicts — stays on the main model. Must be served by the same provider.
settings.ai.disabledHint: Turn AI features on to configure a provider.
settings.ai.probeHint: Sends a one-word prompt through the provider's chat-completions endpoint, to check the selected model itself answers — not just that the server is up.
settings.ai.probeNoStructuredOutput: {{model}} answered, but ignored the requested JSON format. Features that need structured output — commit message, commit plan, daily briefing, history search — will fail on every call with this model.
settings.integrations.gitlab.deviceCodeI: Enter this code on the GitLab page that just opened to authorize Git Manager.
settings.integrations.gitlab.clientIdHin: Self-hosted GitLab keeps its own application registry, so it needs an application registered on that instance (with the device authorization flow enabled). gitlab.com needs nothing here.
